The tables below are the ones \S\ref{sec:sim} summarises.
\texttt{libqueuingsim} is an event-driven simulator in Rust. Its checks
of the propositions run the queues the propositions are stated for
(M/G/1, PS); everything that involves the replica's memory runs the
vLLM~v1 engine's rules, below. The
synthetic checks use $a=2\cdot10^{-5}$, $b=2\cdot10^{-9}$,
$\omega=2\cdot10^{-4}$ and $\beta=2\cdot10^{-9}$ seconds per token
unless a caption says otherwise. Where a miss is paid (rows 8--9 of
Table~\ref{tab:sim-ps}), the eviction and admission experiment
(Tables~\ref{tab:sim-evict-dyn} and~\ref{tab:sim-admission},
Figure~\ref{fig:sim-admission}) and the replays of production sessions
(Tables~\ref{tab:sim-trace}, \ref{tab:sim-trace-price}
and~\ref{tab:sim-trace-split}) use the cost model calibrated on the
testbed (\S\ref{sec:exp-testbed}) and run the replica as programs of
seQ, a language for serving deployments whose interpreter reproduces the
upstream vLLM~v1 scheduler request for request (first-token and
last-token steps, preemptions and cached tokens) on recorded scenarios
and on a full trace replay. Every number is generated by the
simulator from fixed seeds and is a property of the simulated model,
not a measurement; the best value in each comparison is in bold.
